newsitem.title: USA: Judge OKs $90 mln in law fees in Prudential case.
newsitem.headline: Judge OKs $90 mln in law fees in Prudential case.

text.p: U.S. District Court Judge Alfred Wolin on Thursday approved $90 million in lawyers' fees in the class action suit filed against Prudential Insurance Co of America.
Judge Wolin granted immediate payment of $45 million to a battery of attorneys involved in the suit.
Wolin said the remaining $45 million will be paid once the 330,000 claims against Prudential are satisfied.
Wolin said in no case shall the attorneys' fees exceed $90 million.
Prudential Insurance spokesman Robert De Fillippo said the company has "not disputed the amount of the lawyers' fees."
Prudential Insurance Co has been charged with misleading policyholders over a 13-year period.
The class action suit affects 10.7 million life insurance policyholders and is expected to cost Prudential anywhere from $410 million to $2 billion dollars.
